title: Insulin Pump Program Fulfillment Standard: Conditions for a Refill Shipment
content:
This standard states when a supply refill on an Insulin Pump Program may leave the warehouse, what it draws on and how it is billed.

## 1. Program status and the authorization drawn

1.1 A refill ships only while the program is active; a program in referral received, pending authorization, on hold or closed receives no refill.

1.2 Each refill draws on one authorization grant of the program, recorded on the shipment, and the ship date must be on or before the valid-through date on the authorization being drawn.

1.3 The units shipped may not exceed the program's authorized units remaining. The supply days of a shipment are the tier's supply days per shipment, shortened to the whole 30-day blocks that remain before the authorization's valid-through date when fewer remain. *This supply-days clause is no longer in force for an infusion-set refill or for a cartridge or reservoir refill, each of which takes its supply days from its own current refill rule; it remains in force for every other refill of the program.* The units and pieces follow from the supply days under the product's quantity rules.

## 2. Customer confirmation and reminders

2.1 On tiers where refill confirmation is required, the refill ships only after the customer personally confirms, for this shipment, that they are still using the item and how much supply they have on hand. *This confirmation clause is no longer in force for an infusion-set refill or for a cartridge or reservoir refill, whose confirmation follows its own current refill rule; it remains in force for every other refill of the program.*

2.2 On those tiers the confirmation date is recorded on the shipment, Larkfield never ships those tiers automatically, and Larkfield's own refill reminder for those tiers is made no sooner than the tier's refill reminder lead time in calendar days before the planned ship date.

2.3 On the self-pay tier refills ship on the subscription schedule without a per-shipment confirmation.

## 3. Earliest ship date of the next refill

The next refill of the same item ships no earlier than the tier's refill ship lead time in calendar days before the end of the supply of the previous refill shipment of that item, counted in calendar days: the previous refill's ship date plus its supply days gives the end of its supply, the earliest permitted ship date is that many calendar days before that end date, and shipping on that earliest date is allowed. A replacement shipment never counts as the previous refill.

| Hypothetical case (previous refill shipped on day S with 90 supply days; ship lead 10 days) | Result |
|---|---|
| End of supply | day S plus 90 |
| Earliest permitted ship date | day S plus 80 |
| Refill on day S plus 80 | permitted |
| Refill on day S plus 79 | too early |

## 4. Coverage verification

The coverage record the program bills must have been verified with the payer within the tier's coverage reverification period in calendar months before the ship date, as shown by the coverage record's last verified date; the self-pay tier has no coverage to verify. A last verified date falling exactly on the edge of that period still satisfies the test; one day older does not.

## 5. Shipping charges and billing

5.1 Standard ground shipping is free on insured tiers; on the self-pay tier standard shipping costs the tier's standard shipping fee, posted as a patient charge, unless the shipment's cash-price total reaches the free-shipping threshold.

5.2 Expedited shipping is provided on the customer's request for the expedited shipping fee, posted as a patient charge because no payer covers delivery speed, and is recorded as expedited at no charge when the expedite only makes up for a delay Larkfield caused.

5.3 A refill on a payer tier is billed to the payer by claim with the ship date as the date of service; a refill on the self-pay tier is charged to the customer at the Larkfield cash price.

## 6. Inpatient stays

On tiers where an inpatient hold is required, nothing ships while the customer is an inpatient in a hospital or skilled nursing facility; the program is held under the program hold rules.
